title: 1Password Security Breach: What Was Accessed and What Wasn't
summary: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account had been breached and began investigating. The company says the breached GitHub account was used to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, with the code downloading some customer data. Here's a list of what the hacker was able to get: Names and email addresses customers use to sign into 1Password Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times Public keys Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (1Password says this can't be used for account access) Tokens in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery Other non-secret account data related to 1Password's internal architecture, like version numeric identifiers and file numeric identifiers 1Password source code, which 1Password says does not include customer data or user secrets Access to 1Password's CI/CD system, which it says has infrastructure-related secrets for the service to work According to 1Password, there is no impact to its services, availability, or product security. Customer vaults and the items in them were not accessed, nor were the keys that protect vaults. The hacker did not have access to account recovery keys or 1Password apps and browser extensions. 1Password vaults are encrypted and protected by keys on the user end, so content is not accessible to 1Password or anyone who hacks the 1Password servers. The biggest risk comes from the token breach. Tokens can be used for account recovery, but they only work when paired with an SSO sign-in or a six-digit code sent to a user's email address. Codes have now been changed from six numeric digits to 10 alphanumeric characters to make them more difficult to brute force. The affected GitHub account has been disabled, and the attacker's token was revoked. Internal credentials that may have been exposed have been revoked. Internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls have been "tightened," with new detection methods for similar attacks. The company found no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using the exposed account provisioning tokens, and it has hired independent cybersecurity experts to validate its response. 1Password users who had a token accessed were notified, but it is unclear if 1Password has sent notices about the breach to all users. While the blog post is titled as "update on" a security incident, it does not seem that the breach was disclosed when 1Password first learned of it six days ago. 1Password will not contact users to ask for an account password or Secret Key, and the information should be entered only in the official 1Password app or official website. It recommends all users be cautious about phishing attempts like emails, texts, and calls that mention 1Password or account recovery. Users do not need to update or change anything in their 1Password accounts. title: iPhone 18 Pro Max Battery Exhausts a Toy Cyclops in New Apple Ad
summary: Apple today shared a fun ad highlighting the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery, which offers the longest battery life ever in an iPhone. In the spot, a cyclops toy comes to life and becomes enamored with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max. The toy takes photos, plays games, uses apps, listens to music, captures videos, makes calls, watches TV, and uses the flashlight for shadow puppets. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts through all of it, remaining at half charge when the cyclops's battery dies and the toy falls asleep. Apple's ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max lasts up to 30 hours in "typical use," which is based on median iPhone usage. The metric includes messages, photo taking, music, social app use, streaming, games, browsing, and navigation. The device lasts for up to 40 hours when streaming video, and up to 45 hours when watching downloaded videos. title: Redesigned OLED MacBook Air Could Launch in 2027 or 2028
summary: A MacBook Air with a new look could launch in late 2027 or 2028, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman said in the latest episode of his Power On podcast. Apple plans to refresh the ‌MacBook Air‌ with M6 chips in early 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2, but that update won't include a new design. A more extensive overhaul could follow later in 2027 or in 2028, and the ‌MacBook Air‌ could get an OLED display at that time. MacBook Air is Apple's most popular computer, and they need to keep it very fresh. And so my anticipation is 2027, 2028 is when we're going to get the big MacBook Air overhaul. And I think OLED will be part of that conversation. Apple last overhauled the ‌MacBook Air‌'s design in 2022, eliminating the prior wedge shape for a more uniform MacBook Pro-style chassis. The machine adopted a brighter Liquid Retina display with a notch for the camera, and a MagSafe charging port. In 2023, Apple added a 15-inch model, but since then, we've only gotten minor updates. Apple just added ‌OLED‌ to the MacBook Pro with the launch of the 2026 PROLED models, so it's not clear whether the high-end display will trickle down to the ‌MacBook Air‌ that quickly. In prior reports , Gurman has leaned more toward the 2028 timeline than late 2027. Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899, while the ‌MacBook Air‌ is one of Apple's more affordable notebooks and starts at $1,299. Apple would likely need to offer a high-end ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Air‌ alongside ‌MacBook Air‌ models with an LCD display to keep the price gap intact. title: Rumor: iOS 28 to Revamp Notifications
summary: Earlier today, we resurfaced a longstanding issue with Apple not consistently enforcing its rules related to iPhone apps advertising through notifications . It is a good time to share that we heard from multiple sources that Apple is planning to revamp the iPhone's notification system with iOS 28 next year. The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details. This is just a rumor. On Android 16 and later, you can filter notifications into News, Promotions, Social, and Suggested categories, and an equivalent iOS option if implemented would help to hide advertising clutter. title: WhatsApp Finally Adds Scheduled Messages
summary: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a message can be done by pressing and holding the send button after composing and then choosing a date and time. Scheduled messages work with text, photos, and videos, and will still send even if a user's device is offline. There is an option to see all scheduled messages and delete them before they're sent if needed. Scheduled messages are end-to-end encrypted and look like any other WhatsApp message, with no indication on the receiver's end that the message was scheduled. Apple's iMessage service already has a Send Later feature that supports scheduling messages, so WhatsApp is catching up with Apple's built-in messaging option. WhatsApp says scheduled messages are rolling out globally over the coming weeks.
